Note: This Review is Non-Biased and Not Affiliated with MidJourney.

In this article, we will give you an in-depth breakdown of the AI Image Generator, MidJourney V7.

Midjourney V7 creates painterly, cinematic images with detailed brushstrokes, rich colors, and film-style lighting. Its results resemble high-resolution stills from an art film or a painting.

  • Native Resolution: 2048 × 2048 pixels

  • Optional 4K Upscale: Up to 4096 × 4096 pixels.

  • Average Generation Speed: Typically under 20 seconds per image

Even though Midjourney is one of the most loved AI Image generators on the market, it definitely has its flaws.

MidJourney V7 - Benchmark Score (8.62/10)

In our Curious Refuge Labs™ review, Midjourney was scored across three categories: Prompt Adherence, Visual Fidelity, and Style & Realism. The average scores were:

  • Prompt Adherence: 9.2/10

  • Visual Fidelity: 8.31/10

  • Style & Realism: 8.34/10

  • Total Curious Refuge Labs™ Score: 8.62/10

Midjourney V7’s overall score reflects a model that delivers consistently strong results even under varied testing conditions. It isn’t perfect, but V7 is an obedient, balanced, and production-ready image generator.

MidJourney V7 | AI Image Expert Review

We evaluated V7 using our 29-image benchmark. Each category was scored for Prompt Adherence, Visual Fidelity, and Style & Realism.

The results were strong in portraits, natural settings, and human anatomy, but V7 struggled with precise text, accurate physics, and repeating patterns.

Prompt Adherence — 9.2/10

In the three examples below, the model follows the prompt with near-surgical precision. That’s because these prompts contain: one subject (or one action), one lighting setup, and one environment.

With no competing elements vying for priority, the model can devote its full “budget” to reproducing the exact pose, angle, texture, and lighting described in the prompt.




That same discipline extends into large, real-world environments. The two aerial shots below both demonstrate a strong grasp of composition, organizing the frame into a coherent foreground, middle ground, and background while preserving correct scale, depth, and colors/gradients.

Your subject can be human or environmental, but it comes down to one focal point (cliffs), one light source (the sun), and one location (the coastline). The content of your prompt matters less than the structure of the scene being described.

Visual Fidelity — 8.31/10

Structure gives the model something to hold onto, but structure alone doesn’t guarantee realism. The most reliable way to get lifelike results in Midjourney is to either tighten your focal point or pull the shot dramatically wide.

We see the strongest fidelity in extreme close-ups, and while wide environmental scenes are strong, their fidelity still lags behind macro shots.

In the extreme close-up, pores, irises, and tiny hairs are crystal clear because the prompt focuses the model on minute details.

The shot of the bee shows the same effect: pollen, micro-hairs, and tiny reflective surfaces are sharp because nothing competes for that fidelity “budget.”

For creators, that means tightly framed shots are where Midjourney behaves most like a high-end DSLR camera.

The model renders the broad strokes, body, ground, and trees, but it fails on small details like hair and grass.

Overall, Midjourney achieves its highest Visual Fidelity when one clear central subject is lit by a single clear source, inside a simple frame.

Style & Realism — 8.34/10

Midjourney favors a polished, cinematic look with clean lighting, controlled contrast, and pleasing color harmony, even if the prompt doesn't ask for it.

In techspeak, we’d call that a model’s “prior aesthetic,” and Midjourney’s is filmic, cinematic.

In simple shots like the ones shown below, the bias helps, giving a polished, cinematic look that feels art-directed. But sometimes it creates images that are overly idealized or too polished.



Where this cinematic bias becomes most obvious is in scenes involving physics or unpredictable motion. In the explosion shot below, the flame texture and color palette look straight out of an action film, but the blast expands too symmetrically to be physically accurate.

The explosion is just a little too perfect to be believable.

The coffee pour shot below shows a similar pattern: the mug, wood grain, and reflections are rendered beautifully, while the coffee stream behaves like an idealized ribbon rather than a chaotic liquid.



Even the bonfire above leans into stylization, producing elegant ember trails that prioritize visual appeal over chaotic realism.

Midjourney’s Style & Realism lean cinematic: it softens disorder, lights scenes like a movie set, and favors polished visuals over exact physical accuracy.

Do We Recommend MidJourney V7 for AI Artists?

Yes, with important caveats. Midjourney V7 is great for AI artists who need high-quality stills, consistent characters, good lighting, and cinematic framing. It struggles with realistic physics, accurate text, and precise multi-object scenes, so it’s not an all-in-one tool.

Still, it’s one of the best for generating frames, storyboards, and visual development.

How Does MidJourney V7 Stack Up Against Other AI Image Tools?

MidJourney V7 posts a strong showing across our testing, but it still falls short of the current leader. Nana Banana Pro, for reference, scored 9.5 overall, giving it a measurable edge in precision and consistency. V7 remains artistic, powerful, and highly capable, but it isn’t the top performer.

Caption: 

**Welcome back! **Picture this: You're a contractor for OpenAI, and they just asked you to raid your old work folders. That PowerPoint deck you made for a work itinerary? The Excel model from your last finance gig? Send it over—well, strip out the confidential stuff first. 

This is how OpenAI is [preparing](https://www.wired.com/story/openai-contractor-upload-real-work-documents-ai-agents/) its AI agents for the real world. Not with sanitized test cases or academic benchmarks, but with the actual messy artifacts of knowledge work. We're talking about a fundamental rewiring of how companies operate. Are you ready for 2026? Because we’re just getting started.

----------
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/cbebdca9-8ecb-4ecc-83ee-58993a37c075/1127_Header_v3_Line.png?t=1701202240)

Caption: 

----------
### **Apple Hands Siri's Brain to Google**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/6f858e9f-4b12-4fa6-a3b3-5e3841961682/image.png?t=1768368872)
Caption: Via The Information

After years of watching from the sidelines, Apple is [making](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/12/apple-google-ai-siri-gemini.html) a big AI move: a multiyear deal with Google to power the next generation of Siri using Gemini models. 

**What's happening:** 

* **Apple **🤝 **Google:** Apple will lean on Google's Gemini and cloud infrastructure for its foundation models, though processing will still happen on-device and through Apple's private cloud compute. 

* **Siri’s struggles:** The deal comes after Apple delayed its Siri AI upgrade from 2025 to 2026, struggling to deliver on features it had already started advertising. 

* **The lead up:** Google was reportedly in talks for this since August, with Bloomberg suggesting Apple could pay around $1 billion annually for the partnership.

**The OpenAI complication:** Apple already integrates ChatGPT into Siri for complex queries that need broader world knowledge. Apple says it's not changing the OpenAI agreement, but the message is clear: When it came time to build the core intelligence layer, Apple chose Google.

**Validation for Google:** After lagging OpenAI in mindshare for two years, Google is now winning the trust (and checkbooks) of the world's most cautious tech company. The partnership signals Google, not OpenAI, is the partner Apple trusts the most.

“**The bigger picture:**** **Apple's legendary control-freak instincts are giving way to pragmatism. In the AI era, even the most self-reliant companies are realizing they need partners to compete and can't build cutting-edge AI alone.“ — 


--------------------
### **Microsoft Promises Your Power Bill Won't Pay for AI**

Microsoft [made](https://techcrunch.com/2026/01/13/microsoft-announces-glut-of-new-data-centers-but-says-it-wont-let-your-electricity-bill-go-up/) a public pledge that sounds almost too good to be true: As it builds out massive new data centers for AI, it won't let your electricity bill go up. The announcement comes amid growing backlash against data center construction.

**What Microsoft is promising:** The company says it will "pay its own way" by working with utility companies and state commissions to ensure the cost of powering its data centers isn't passed on to residential customers. It's also pledging to create local jobs and minimize water usage. 

**Community pushback:** 142 activist groups across 24 states are organizing against data center projects. Microsoft has already abandoned plans for a Wisconsin facility in October after overwhelmingly negative community feedback. Meanwhile, Meta announced its own AI infrastructure program just one day before Microsoft's pledge, signaling that major AI companies are coming to the same realization—that the social license to build AI infrastructure isn't guaranteed.

“**The bigger picture: **AI's infrastructure demands are colliding with local reality. These facilities require enormous amounts of electricity and water, often in communities that didn't ask for them and won't directly benefit from the AI services they power.“ —

 CONTEXT IS THE NEW MOAT (9 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 Different teams can use the same model but get different results. The

mouth. On the retention side, AI is commoditizing the value props most

Update ComfyUI version to > 0.7.0
Search the “Kling Motion Control“ node
Prepare your own reference image and reference video, and run this example workflow
Best Practices
 Match character proportions: Ensure full-body/half-body in the image matches the motion reference
